menu.generalIntro:
At Kuju Nonohana no Sato, local ingredients always come first.
Our mountain-vegetable tempura, foraged in the hills and fried fresh each morning, is prized for its aroma and its place in traditional herbal cooking.
We are just as particular about the miso and soy sauce that good cooking depends on.
Both are fine seasonings developed together with the producers who make them.
menu.groupIntro:
As more people look for food that is good for them, we stay with the seasonal ingredients Japanese households have long relied on, above all the wild mountain vegetables valued in traditional herbal cooking.
Some are barely a step from wild herbs, and we believe the hardy vitality of such plants becomes a source of our own energy.
notes: The menu may change with the season.
Some items may be unavailable depending on ingredient supply.
Please let us know in advance if you have any allergies.
groupNotes: We can also arrange kaiseki banquet courses to suit your budget.
From small groups to large parties, and for celebrations, memorial gatherings and banquets of any size, we are happy to discuss both budget and menu.
Dishes may change with the season.
Please tell us when booking if you have allergies or ingredients you would rather avoid.
Course menus must be reserved by the day before.
Please let us know of any cancellation by the day before.
